newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Public, institutions buy IBM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Public, institutions buy IBM.

text.p: A rally in shares of blue chip International Business Machines Corp drew public and institutional investors to the options on Wednesday.
Even so, traders said the activity was relatively quiet.
"In a sense, for a rally it's kind of slow," said a trader in the IBM pit on the CBOE, blaming the sluggish action on summer doldrums.
"Generally, for this type of move, it's been slower than usual."
IBM shares were up 3-3/4 at 115-1/2 on Wednesday afternoon after Salomon Brothers upgraded the stock.
The brokerage firm raised its rating to strong buy from buy and set a 12-month target of $145.
The most active IBM options were the September 120 call with 3,976 contracts traded, the September 115 call with 2,686 and the September 110 put with 1,322.
"It's been active but it's settled down into a range," the trader said of IBM options activity. He added that both retail and institutional investors were doing the IBM business.
In other trading, Philip Morris Cos Inc options continued active, this time helped by news of a dividend increase.

The stock and its options had been active recently as the stock fell on news of a jury verdict against several tobacco companies and then rebounded on news of a verdict in their favor in a separate case.

But on Wednesday, the company announced a 20 percent increase in its quarterly dividend, to $1.20. In late afternoon trading, the stock was down 1/4 at 91-5/8 after rising as high as 93-3/4. Turnover topped 3.3 million shares.
Traders said the dividend increase was widely expected, but kept investors attracted to the options, which moved little.
"I think this was not unexpected," Marty Kearney at PTI Securities said of the dividend rise.
"Volatilities are pretty much at historic levels," he said of the options.

Calls were active right through the March 1997 series, while most put activity was centered in the September, October and January 1997 series. The Philip Morris September 90 call was the most active, with volume of 2,692 by late trade. The option was down 3/8 at 3-1/8.
The September 95 call traded 1,769.
Other actives included the September 90 put, which traded 1,687 contracts and the October 100 call, which traded about 1,000 contracts.
The January 1997 90 put traded about 1,050 contracts.
Also, WorldCom Inc and MFS Communications Co Inc options continued to attract attention, two days after WorldCom said it would acquire MFS in a deal valued at $14 billion.
The two stocks topped the Nasdaq active list, with WorldCom losing one to 20 and MFS dropping 2-1/16 to 39-1/4.
